label: copy-phase input p late in the copy, strongest when outputting y
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and only when the fed-back input token is p (99.9% of activations, 100% of mass). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on any other input token apart from 6 activations on y. It needs a late copy position: it is almost silent for recall_idx <= 2, and the rate rises with recall_idx and with L (L=9 holds 52% of mass). Magnitude depends strongly on the token being output: out_tok y gives 18.6x lift and 48% of mass, and every top example is p->y. Next come g, q, t and p. Even so, it fires on only ~10% of copy-phase p inputs at recall_idx >= 3, so precision is limited. Dev scores: p & recall_idx>=3 alone gives recall 0.99 at precision 0.10; adding out_tok in {y,g,q,t,p} gives precision 0.39, recall 0.68, mass 0.80; out_tok==y alone gives precision 0.89, recall 0.31, mass 0.48. Many weak activations (<0.1 of max) remain with other output tokens.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=p (+8.04), in_tok=p (+3.44), phase=2 & out_tok=q (+3.21), phase=2 & out_tok=y (+3.02), next_out=y (+3.02), out_tok=y (+2.82). Lower it: recall_idx=1 (-3.37), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.37), phase=2 & out_tok=v (-3.36), out_tok=o (-2.97).
